title: EV charging in Germany | VOOL
description: VOOL chargers and load management in Germany: local partners, grants and rules, and datasheets.

sections.title: EV charging for buildings in Germany, on the connection they already have
sections.lead: Chargers, load management and billing from one maker. Sold and installed by 1 partner in Germany.

sections.title: Grants and rules in Germany
paragraphs: Two things shape a project in a German apartment building: funding and metering law.
points: Funding: a federal programme for charging in multi-family buildings, with up to €2,000 per charging point, opened on 15 April 2026. Applications were accepted until 10 November 2026. Check for a follow-up programme and for state and municipal funding.

Billing by the kWh: when several users are billed from the same charging point, German metering and calibration law (Mess- und Eichrecht) applies in addition to MID. Talk to us before you plan billed charging.
Company cars at home: since January 2026 electricity costs are reimbursed by the exact kWh, so a meter is needed.

items.title: Apartment buildings
items.text: Many chargers on the existing main fuse, with each resident paying for their own charging.

items.title: Offices and fleets
items.text: Employees pay for private charging; company cars are reported separately.

items.title: Developers
items.text: Design charging into new buildings and size the connection smaller.

items.title: Sell or install VOOL in Germany
items.text: We are adding partners in this market.

items.q: Does VOOL have an Eichrecht-certified charger?
items.a: Not today. A MID version is coming in 2027. Ask us what fits your billing model.
No. Local partners sell and install. VOOL makes the hardware and software and supports the partners.
From 1 January 2027 newly installed chargers in the EU must support ISO 15118-20. The new VOOL Charger does.

sections.title: Planning charging in Germany?
sections.lead: Send us the parking spaces and the main fuse size. We reply within 1–2 working days.
